newsitem.title: UK: West African crude moves into Med as margins jump.
newsitem.headline: West African crude moves into Med as margins jump.

text.p: Strong gas oil prices in Europe and a weak WTI/Brent spread have driven more West African crude into the Mediterranean, traders said on Wednesday.
But the arbitrage was not depressing the value of local sweet crudes, which were also rising relative to Dated Brent, they added.

Mediterranean refiners buy a few West African cargoes every month, but recently the flow has increased and dealers estimate that five or six cargoes have been sold to France, Spain and Italy. A jump in refining margins, especially for gas oil-rich crude, was largely responsible for the demand spike, they said.

Gas oil-rich Forcados was particularly favoured and traded at a stronger Dated Brent +48 cents this week. This strength was reflected in the October NNPC contract prices, released on Wednesday, which showed a 13-cent rise in Forcados to Dated Brent +36 cents.

Traders said the NNPC changes were broadly in line with the market, although some complained that they left very little margin for profit after 8-10 cent costs. One said the 18-cent increase in Bonny Medium to Dated +28 cents was excessive.
Nigeria's other crudes were cut by 2-9 cents.

Sweet Mediterranean crudes were also benefiting from increased refiner demand, dealers said, and Algeria's Sonatrach issued an opening offer of Dated Brent +70 cents for its October liftings, versus 61 cents in September. This follows a Tunisian Zarzaitine sale at Dated +65/70 cents this week.
Algerian contract holders said they would be asking for prices to be left unchanged.
Sour crude in the Mediterranean was stable, with very few cargoes left in September and October programmes still undecided.
Syria's Sytrol opened its October price talks with an offer of Dated Brent -30 cents for its Light crude, 10 cents above September. Buyers countered with bids 20 cents below that.
"Most buyers would accept a rollover," a trader said.
Sytrol's offer for October Souedie liftings was Dated Brent -$2.85 per barrel, unchanged from September.
Russian Urals was valued at Dated Brent -80 cents cif Augusta, following Monday's distressed sale at -90 cents, as only one or two cargoes were still available in September.
